rationale: The literature presents real evidence both supporting and conflicting with the hypothesis that multi-gene 17q24.2 microdeletions involving both PSMD12 and BPTF confer an augmented phenotype with significantly higher rates of postnatal microcephaly and craniofacial severity. On the supporting side, BPTF haploinsufficiency was established to cause postnatal microcephaly in 7/9 individuals, speech delay (10/10), and craniofacial anomalies in both humans and zebrafish (Stankiewicz et al., 2017), leading authors to propose blended/compound phenotypes in contiguous 17q24.2 microdeletions spanning both genes (Stankiewicz et al., 2017; Hancarova et al., 2018; Isidor et al., 2022). Conversely, Küry et al. (2017) documented microcephaly in most subjects with de novo PSMD12 disruption alone, and Isidor et al. (2022) highlighted substantial variable expressivity across 24 patients with isolated PSMD12 single-nucleotide variants versus copy-number deletions, arguing that PSMD12 haploinsufficiency itself drives the core neurodevelopmental and craniofacial spectrum without a definitive statistical difference demonstrated between isolated PSMD12 truncating variants and contiguous deletions.

evidence.text: BPTF loss-of-function and missense variants cause developmental delay/intellectual disability (10/10), speech delay (10/10), postnatal microcephaly (7/9), and dysmorphic features (9/10). Zebrafish bptf mutants showed reduced head size and abnormal craniofacial patterning, leading to the hypothesis that individuals with contiguous 17q24.2 deletions affecting both PSMD12 and BPTF present blended phenotypes.

evidence.text: Review of 17q24.2-q24.3 microdeletions noted that clinical features and genotype-phenotype correlations relate to the joint contributions of PSMD12 and BPTF, with microcephaly tracking more specifically with BPTF involvement.

evidence.text: In an expanded cohort of 24 unrelated patients with Stankiewicz-Isidor syndrome caused by either single nucleotide truncating variants or copy-number deletions involving PSMD12, expressivity of features was highly variable and driven fundamentally by PSMD12 haploinsufficiency, demonstrating that isolated PSMD12 variants are sufficient to produce the recognizable syndromic phenotype.

conflicts: Küry et al. (2017) observed microcephaly in most individuals with isolated PSMD12 disruption, whereas Stankiewicz et al. (2017) suggested microcephaly is more specifically attributed to BPTF disruption.

Isidor et al. (2022) noted high phenotypic variability among patients harboring isolated truncating SNVs versus larger CNV deletions of PSMD12, failing to establish a statistically significant augmentation in microcephaly or facial dysmorphism severity strictly attributable to concurrent BPTF haploinsufficiency.

new_directions.question_text: Does head circumference standard deviation score differ significantly between carriers of isolated PSMD12 loss-of-function SNVs and contiguous 17q24.2 deletions encompassing BPTF?
new_directions.rationale: Directly testing OFC z-scores between molecular subgroups will resolve whether BPTF codeletion worsens microcephaly quantitatively.

new_directions.question_text: Do double-heterozygous knockout cellular/animal models (psmd12+/- ; bptf+/-) exhibit synergistic defects in neural progenitor proliferation and apoptosis over single heterozygotes?
new_directions.rationale: Modeling both genes together will reveal whether their haploinsufficiency has an additive, synergistic, or epistatic effect on neurodevelopment.
